name: CoAuth
description: Agent-native prior-authorization cockpit. Exposes WebMCP tools so an AI agent can complete a health-insurance prior authorization together with a human clinician.

whenToUse.summary: Use CoAuth when a user needs to prepare, check, or submit a health-insurance prior authorization (especially for a specialty/biologic drug) with a clinician kept in the loop.
bestFor: Start a prior authorization for a patient, drug, and payer
Check a prior authorization for denial risk before submitting
Find what is missing or malformed in a prior authorization
Draft a medical-necessity statement grounded in the chart
Draft an appeal letter for a denied prior authorization
notFor: Submitting without a clinician - submit is blocked until a human signs
Fabricating clinician-judgment fields or overriding contraindications
whenToUse.howToCall: Open the page in an agentic browser and call the WebMCP tools starting with get_workflow_guidance, or call the read-only MCP server for data tools.

mcp.note: These three tools are the read-only data surface: patient records, payer coverage rules and validation. The interactive workspace tools (filling fields, drafting clinician text, submitting) are exposed in the page via WebMCP, because they act on a live workspace that only exists in the browser. Submission always requires a clinician signature and cannot be performed over MCP.

safety.notes: submit is blocked until a human clinician signs. Agents must not fabricate clinician-judgment fields or resolve critical clinical conflicts.
